answers.explanation: The passage describes the threats to the planet's environment, which are environmentally induced risks.
The passage says poverty makes people in developing countries degrade the environment, such as overgrazing and cutting trees, to survive.
The passage says a forest the size of Sierra Leone disappears each year, which is colossal.
The passage says the richer countries are responsible because most commercial energy is produced there.
The writer urges cooperation to protect the natural environment, which is the central message.
The passage argues that economists should admit the census figures carry a margin of error.
The passage says lack of accurate population figures adversely affects policies, so precise figures are needed for policy implementation.
The contentious subject is the sharing of the federation account, which is based on population figures.
The UPE example shows how unreliable population information misled planners.
The writer calls the census effort worthwhile, which shows an optimistic view of solving the problem.
The writer describes a picture of a man, a beggar.
The writer says the man must not have been more than thirty, and the signs of youth support this assessment of his age.
Beggars is used as an exclamatory noun naming the people.
The writer describes the human waste as the consequence of young women and girls becoming pregnant through irresponsible men.
The passage is about young men and female beggars.
Dictionaries supply information about a language.
The dictionary, context and word analysis contribute to forming meaning.
The use of dictionaries is to be encouraged.
Students should not jeopardize fluency by considering every word.
Lexical items may obstruct meaning, which is the sense of may.
Glossing over words is not sufficient practice to encourage dictionary use.
The skill must be built into the reading text.
Excessive reliance on the dictionary replaces contextual reading.
The argument is that allowing students to guess is a discovery method.
A discovery method is a teaching method for enlarging understanding.
